pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis THE SMOKING GUN: An unrecognized mature ovarian teratoma containing neural tissue, triggering autoantibody production against N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The condition is an autoimmune encephalitis caused by IgG antibodies targeted against the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor. In many young female patients, ectopic neural tissue within an ovarian teratoma triggers the immune system to synthesize cross-reactive autoantibodies. These antibodies pass through the blood-brain barrier and cause cross-linking and internalisation of surface NMDA receptors on GABAergic interneurons. The resulting severe reduction of NMDA receptor function disinhibits downstream pathways, causing a hyperdopaminergic state that produces progressive psychiatric symptoms, characteristic orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic instability, hypoventilation, and catatonia.
